messages.content: The Seattle relatives still have not confirmed whether they can fit us Wednesday night. Compare leaving after school Wednesday with going early Thursday for all three of us, and make sure the Sunday return gets us home at a reasonable hour.

I found two workable outbound strategies for November 26 or 27, with Sunday, November 30 returns. I’ll compare total cost and usable time in Seattle, including a Wednesday hotel night where needed. Should I keep this to nonstop flights, or include a connection if it materially lowers the fare?
Use the nonstop options for this comparison. There is no point saving a little if we lose more of the short visit in an airport.

The strongest Wednesday option is Alaska 329, leaving ORD at 6:35 p.m. and arriving SEA at 9:05 p.m. The fare is $612 per person in main cabin, or $1,836 for three. With deplaning and the ride into the city, expect to reach a hotel around 10:15-10:45 p.m. A cancellable room near the relatives is about $238 including tax, bringing the Wednesday strategy to $2,074 before local transportation.
What is the best Thursday flight? I do not want to call it a five-night visit if the first night is just a late hotel check-in.

United 2091 leaves ORD Thursday at 7:10 a.m. and arrives SEA at 9:45 a.m., nonstop. It is $529 per person, or $1,587 for three. Allowing for the airport and ground transportation, you should reach the relatives around 11:15 a.m. That avoids the hotel and is $487 less than the Wednesday plan, but it requires leaving home around 4:45 a.m.
So Wednesday really buys us only the morning, since everyone will be asleep when we arrive. Show me Sunday before deciding.

Two nonstop Sunday returns fit the Monday constraint. United 2216 leaves SEA at 1:20 p.m. and reaches ORD at 7:18 p.m.; paired with either outbound, it is included in the totals already quoted. Alaska 328 leaves at 3:55 p.m. and arrives ORD at 9:48 p.m. It adds $96 total for the family and gives you about two and a half more hours in Seattle, but likely puts you home around 11:00 p.m.
Use the earlier Sunday flight in both comparisons. Owen has school Monday, and Daniel and I both need to be functional for work.

With the 1:20 p.m. Sunday return held constant: Wednesday travel costs about $2,074 with the estimated hotel, gives you Thursday morning free in Seattle, and means roughly four useful family days plus that morning. Thursday travel costs $1,587, reaches the relatives around 11:15 a.m., and gives you roughly three and a half useful family days. Both return to Chicago at 7:18 p.m. Sunday, with an estimated home arrival around 8:30-9:00 p.m.
Is there a later Wednesday departure that costs less? We cannot leave for O'Hare until about 4:30 after school.

American 2367 leaves ORD at 8:05 p.m. and arrives SEA at 10:38 p.m., nonstop, at $574 per person. That saves $114 across three tickets versus the 6:35 p.m. flight, but hotel arrival would be around midnight. With the same $238 room, the trip total is about $1,960, still $373 more than Thursday. Leaving home at 4:30 should provide a reasonable airport margin for the 8:05 departure.

Thursday looks better unless the relatives say Wednesday night is available. Keep the 7:10 Thursday outbound and 1:20 Sunday return as the leading plan. If they can host us Wednesday, compare that 8:05 flight again without the hotel.

The leading plan is now United 2091 on Thursday, November 27, ORD 7:10 a.m. to SEA 9:45 a.m., returning on United 2216 Sunday, November 30, SEA 1:20 p.m. to ORD 7:18 p.m., for $1,587 total for Marcus, Daniel, and Owen. Nothing has been booked. If Wednesday lodging with the relatives becomes available, the backup is American 2367, ORD 8:05 p.m. to SEA 10:38 p.m.; without a hotel, that itinerary would total about $1,722 with the same Sunday return, $135 more than Thursday, while preserving Thursday morning in Seattle.
